newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: CANTV closes up 12 pct on Caracas bolsa.
newsitem.headline: CANTV closes up 12 pct on Caracas bolsa.

text.p: Venezuelan telephone company CANTV VNT.N closed at 1727.00 bolivars ($3.67) on the Caracas bolsa, up 11.6 percent from Thursday's pricing at 1,546.80 bolivars ($3.29).
Trading volume was 788,000 shares. The newly-issued stock was slighly off its opening price of 1747.50 bolivars.

CANTV's newly-issued American Depositary Receipts also began trading Friday on the New York Stock Exchange with an opening price of $26. One ADR represented seven Class D shares. At mid-afternoon in New York the ADRs were up $2-7/8 at $25-7/8. They were priced on Thursday at $23.
The government this week completed the sale of its 49 percent stake in CANTV, raising some $1 billion.
The start of trade in the 73 million shares offered on the domestic market was marred by confusion over a complicated scheme that allowed brokers to trade only 20 percent of allotted stock.
Domestic trade was originally slated to begin in December.
"Truthfully, the bolsa wasn't fully prepared for any trade to begin today," said Financorp broker Edwin Escalona.
Brokers nevertheless saw the issue continuing to firm once the full tranche comes on stream next week.
